title: Three-factor beam frontier for product-key state retrieval
question: Can increasing the beam of a three-factor, factor-size-8 product-key recover capability lost at beam 3 while keeping state reranking below the validated two-factor frontier?
hypothesis: Increasing factor beam from 3 to 4 to 5 to 6 should improve proposal coverage and target recall enough to expose a capability/computation frontier, while three-factor addressing retains a substantially smaller candidate fraction than the two-factor factor16/beam6 reference.

arms.name: three_factor_8_beam4
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 4

arms.name: three_factor_8_beam5
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 5

arms.name: three_factor_8_beam6
arms.intervention: three-factor product-key addressing with factor size 8 and beam 6

endpoints.name: target_recall_retention_ratio
endpoints.definition: selective target recall divided by exhaustive target recall

decision_rule.condition: Report every registered arm separately at every M with exact pooled target counts, target-recall retention ratio, proposal retention, states scored/M, end-to-end success, arithmetic, pair generation, and occupancy.
decision_rule.licenses: a workload-specific three-factor beam capability/computation frontier
decision_rule.does_not_license: universal optimal beam size, semantic retrieval guarantees, asymptotic sublinear scaling, or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: An arm satisfies the capability constraint when target-recall retention ratio is at least 0.90 at every registered M level.
decision_rule.licenses: that the arm meets the pre-registered capability floor on the tested workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: that the arm is generally optimal

decision_rule.condition: Compare eligible three-factor arms to the previously validated two-factor factor16/beam6 reference using states_scored_over_M, while keeping the prior reference values unchanged.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence about whether a three-factor beam increase recovers capability without returning to the prior two-factor candidate fraction

held_constant: same 48 training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
